title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

reports.title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

summary:
Two sisters from Rio Arriba County are suing the city of Española after a traffic stop on July 23. Jaclynn Gonzales, 21, was driving with her 12-year-old sister, identified as DD, when a Flock Safety camera misread their license plate, confusing a final 2 for a 7 and flagging the car as stolen from Rio Rancho. Police pulled them over on Calle Duran, handcuffed both sisters, and placed them in separate police vehicles before realizing the error. Jaclynn asked officers to call their nearby mother to pick up the girl, but they handcuffed the 12-year-old instead.

The lawsuits, filed January 3 in state District Court, seek unspecified damages for anxiety, fear, worry, and restriction of movement. Their attorney, Sheri Raphaelson, also represents Adam Pacheco, who was 17 when he was wrongly stopped and forced to kneel with his hands on his head after being mistaken for an armed robbery suspect. The city and police chief did not respond to requests for comment. The cases will proceed in court.
